question: is the court book the right structure for the $5M, or is Parametric tax-aware L/S better even net of ~1% leverage+fee drag?
headline: On TAX ALONE the two are a near-tie (5yr: L/S ~$309k net vs court book ~$279k), so the decision is NOT a tax decision - it turns on (1) whether our selection alpha is real, (2) the wash-sale interaction cost, (3) leverage in a board-forecast break.

model_A_parametric_LS.assumptions: 175/75 (250% gross), tax alpha 3.5/3.0/2.2/1.6/1.2% decaying, mgmt 50bps, short carry 75bps on the 75% short book
model_A_parametric_LS.note: tax alpha DECAYS hard as basis matures - by yr5 fees+carry nearly eat it; the structure's value is front-loaded and it must keep being fed new capital or reset

model_B_court_book.assumptions: 40-60 names, red-share x depth 30%x15% decaying to 15%x12%, 35% blended tax rate, zero fees
model_B_court_book.note: higher idiosyncratic vol in smallcap/court-band names substitutes for L/S's gross-exposure advantage; no fee drag, no financing

breakeven: selection alpha needs to beat only ~0.12%/yr net for the court book to win on combined grounds - a very low bar, BUT our alpha evidence is 66 sessions and must not be extrapolated

decisive_non_tax_factors.wash_sale_interaction: HIGH COST, under-appreciated: household already runs Parametric singles. A 200-400 name L/S sleeve makes most of the US mid/large universe wash-contaminated for the IBKR book on BOTH sides (their buys kill our losses). Our own harvesting gets materially harder - the two programs are partial substitutes, not clean complements
decisive_non_tax_factors.leverage_vs_our_own_board: 250% gross into a p=0.45 AI-break call is levering into our own forecast; the short leg cushions in a broad selloff but 2000-style value-short squeezes are exactly the tail that hurts L/S; ours is unlevered by doctrine (fairly-paid risk = tails bounded AND unlevered)
decisive_non_tax_factors.capacity_reality: our court cadence produced ~8 courted names/week at peak with 6 REJECTS - the book cannot absorb $5M at courted prices quickly; L/S deploys instantly. TIME-TO-DEPLOY is a genuine L/S advantage and a genuine court-book weakness
decisive_non_tax_factors.knowledge_asset: the court book produces the knowledge graph + Brier record (the actual product per the meta); Parametric produces a tax outcome and nothing else

recommendation: BARBELL, explicitly sized: (1) keep the court book as the ALPHA + knowledge engine at its natural capacity - it fills at courted prices, not on a calendar; (2) if deployment stalls (i.e. courts keep saying 'fair, not cheap' as they did all week), route the RESIDUAL to a tax-aware vehicle rather than letting it sit at 2.55% after-tax in SGOV; (3) if choosing a vehicle, prefer a LONG-ONLY tax-managed direct-index sleeve over the L/S: it captures most of the harvest with none of the leverage, none of the short carry, and a smaller wash surface
open_questions_for_the_principal: what are Parametric's ACTUAL quoted terms for the L/S sleeve (mgmt fee, financing spread, minimum, lockup)?
does the existing Parametric relationship already cover part of the US universe - i.e. what is the current holdings list, for the wash-sale map?
is the $5M's job alpha, tax, or house-funding liquidity by 2027-32? that answer changes the structure more than any modeled basis point
